feedback: The Integrator had to make no controller changes for this geometry beyond keeping the baseline gains, because the evidence does not show oscillation. Iteration 0 (entityR2A) gives the key evidence: all 60 trials ended off_track, each with exactly one line-loss event, and max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m limit while rms_error stayed near 0.025 m. This means the robot tracked well and lost the line at the array's outer reach. With body_width 0.12 the off-track limit is 0.06 m, so the sensor span, not body width, is the binding constraint, as your learning notes say. The proposed ±0.06 m span with 16 mm footprints is the right direction to test. The main risk is a flatter signal near centre, which I have not tuned away because there is no oscillation data to justify it. Next steps depend on the next race. If line_loss_events falls to 0 and max_error stays under 0.06 m on most trials, keep this span. If line_loss_events stays at 1, the span is not the only cause. Then the controller's recovery is the issue, and the 7-sensor 0.02 m array you are considering is the next geometry to try. If progress is still low on the slalom, the forward offset is the next lever, because iteration 0 shows slalom progress of only 0.09.
requested_changes: Keep the ±0.06 m span and 16 mm footprint for this race, since iteration 0 shows line loss at the array edge with max_error just above 0.06 m.
If line_loss_events is still 1 after this race, try a 7-sensor array at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.02 m steps with sensor_size 0.012, so the signal stays continuous across the wider span.
If the robot still reacts late on the slalom (iteration 0 slalom progress 0.09), try forward offset y = 0.02 with the current span.
